headline: Real-world CORRELATE study reports 15.2-month overall survival with first-line PD(L)1 therapy
dek: Stephen V Liu said the CORRELATE analysis linked higher mortality to male sex, poor performance status, lower PD-L1 expression and STK11 or KRAS mutations.
body:
Stephen V Liu, MD, wrote on X about the real-world CORRELATE study, tagging the account @ClinicalLung. The study looked at outcomes with first-line PD(L)1 therapy.

According to Liu's summary, overall survival was 15.2 months and progression-free survival was 6 months.

He said increased mortality was seen in male patients, those with poor performance status, those with lower PD-L1 expression, and those with STK11 or KRAS mutations.

Liu added that the risk of death was much higher in patients with STK11, KEAP1 and KRAS co-mutations.

Liu is chief of Hematology & Oncology at Georgetown and MedStar Georgetown University Hospital, and head of Developmental Therapeutics at the Lombardi Cancer Center.
key_quote: Much higher risk of death with STK11, KEAP1, KRAS co-mutations.
